title: The carpenter (Mark 6:1–6)
hookLine: at home they say isn't this the carpenter, and he could do few miracles there

cards: Nazareth. A small place, where people have known each other a long time. The neighbors remember the boy, the workshop, the family.
Jesus has been teaching, healing and calming storms around the lake, with crowds following. Now he comes home. And home has already decided who he is.
Going back to the place that knew you first can mean being seen as who you were, not who you've become.

teach.b: First, the question. On the sabbath he teaches in the synagogue, and people are astonished. Where did he get all this?
What's this wisdom? Then the astonishment curdles. In the Douay-Rheims: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary".
They list his brothers by name and say his sisters are right here with us. And they were scandalized, Mark says: they stumbled over him. Second, the word carpenter.

teach.h: TEKTON: A BUILDER WITH HIS HANDS.
teach.b: Mark's Greek is tekton, a builder, a craftsman who might work in wood or stone. Mark calls Jesus himself the carpenter; Matthew, telling the same scene, says the carpenter's son.
So the hometown remembered a man who worked with his hands. Catholics honor that hidden work, and keep a feast of Saint Joseph the Worker. And notice: son of Mary, not son of Joseph.
Readers have offered different reasons, and the text doesn't say. Third, the proverb.

teach.h: A PROPHET IN HIS OWN COUNTRY.
teach.b: Jesus answers: "A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and in his own house, and among his own kindred." Fourth, the startling line.

teach.h: HE COULD NOT DO MIRACLES THERE.
teach.b: "And he could not do any miracles there, only that he cured a few that were sick, laying his hands upon them." Could not. Mark doesn't soften it.

teach.h: AND HE WONDERED BECAUSE OF THEIR UNBELIEF.
teach.b: And he wondered at their unbelief. The people who had known him longest were the ones who couldn't see him.

how: Catholics honor Jesus's years of ordinary work in Nazareth, especially on the feast of Saint Joseph the Worker, and some offer their daily work as a prayer.

o: the hometown's name for him: a builder, nothing more
a nickname for a fisherman from the lake
a title for a teacher who builds up the Law

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: a builder in wood or stone

s: Mark calls Jesus himself a carpenter
is not this the carpenter? Matthew, in the same scene, says the carpenter's son.
in Nazareth Jesus did as many miracles as anywhere
Mark says he could not do any miracles there, except heal a few sick.
the hometown crowd was impressed and followed him

games.q: you grew up in Nazareth. the boy who fixed your roof is now teaching in the synagogue, and everyone's talking about his wisdom. what does the town say?
o: he's a prophet; let's follow him.
is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?
games.why: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary" they knew him too well to see him, and he wondered at their unbelief.

practice: Think of someone you see every day and hardly notice anymore: a parent, a partner, a roommate, a coworker, a sibling.

Picture them as a stranger would, meeting them for the first time: what's good in them that you've stopped seeing, and what have they become that you haven't caught up with? If you pray, give thanks for them, as if they were new.

wordCard.voice: The carpenter. What his hometown called Jesus, a builder who worked with his hands, and the label that kept them from seeing him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a builder or craftsman, in wood or stone.
